facts.text: I have a large wound on my lower right leg.
They've been swollen for more than 10 years.
My mother and my brother had similar problems with their legs.
Five years ago I had a confirmed deep vein thrombosis, a blood clot, in my right leg.
Apart from the clot, I don't have any significant medical problems.
I haven't had any recent injuries.

findings.name: leg examination
findings.result: Inspection: large ulcer on the right lower leg; varicose veins. Skin around the wound discolored, with chronic changes such as pigmentation. Palpation: edema in both legs, more pronounced in the right leg.

findings.name: foot pulses
findings.result: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses palpable but diminished in the right leg.

findings.name: Doppler ultrasound of the legs
findings.result: Reflux and obstruction in the superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: WBC within normal limits; hemoglobin within normal limits; platelets within normal limits.

x003.source_text: Inspection: Large ulcer on the right lower leg, presence of varicose veins; Skin: Skin around the wound is discolored with evidence of chronic changes such as pigmentation; Palpation: Edema in both legs, more pronounced in the right leg

x004.source_text: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable but diminished in the right leg

x005.source_text: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

x006.source_text: WBC: Within normal limits; Hemoglobin: Within normal limits; Platelets: Within normal limits

x004: Diminished foot pulses in the right leg are not typical of isolated venous disease (could reflect edema or coexisting arterial disease); kept as given.

leakage.reason: The Doppler result (venous reflux and obstruction) is the objective finding that defines venous insufficiency; it is the test's answer.

source_issues: Right-leg pulses are described as diminished, which points away from a purely venous cause.
notes: The leg's pulse check is kept as its own record (foot pulses) because a doctor requests it separately from inspecting and palpating the leg; inspection, skin and palpation of the leg form one record.
'Denies ... heart disease, or diabetes' (review of systems) are past-history denials (f013, f014); 'recent injuries' is filed under medical_history (f012).
The patient was told he had a DVT ('documented'), so the diagnosis name stays in f006.

Gold aliases include post-thrombotic syndrome (chronic venous insufficiency after a DVT, a more specific form); 'chronic venous disease' and 'venous leg ulcer' are not used (broader / a manifestation).

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with a chronic wound on his right lower leg.
